name: Add, Sort, then Merge
summary: Drop the new interval into the list, sort everything by start, then sweep left to right merging any interval that overlaps the last one kept — reusing the Merge Intervals pattern.
visualizationIntent: init: append the new interval (it pops in) and sort so cells reflow into start order; start an empty merged list. loop: the i cursor visits each interval. check: compare its start to the last merged interval's end; disjoint intervals are appended, overlapping ones extend the last merged interval's end. return: the merged interval list.

lineExplanations.3: Add the new interval to the list so it is merged just like the others.
lineExplanations.4: Sort all intervals by start so overlaps sit next to each other.
lineExplanations.5: Start an empty merged result list.
lineExplanations.6: Visit each interval left to right.
lineExplanations.9: If nothing has been merged yet, this interval starts the result.
lineExplanations.10: Append the first interval to the result.
lineExplanations.12: Otherwise, look at the end of the last merged interval.
lineExplanations.13: If the current interval starts after that end, it does not overlap.
lineExplanations.14: Append the disjoint interval as a new block.
lineExplanations.16: Otherwise they overlap; extend only if this interval reaches further.
lineExplanations.17: Stretch the last merged interval's end to cover this one.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def insert(self, intervals, newInterval): receives the sorted intervals and the interval to insert.
syntaxExplanations.3: intervals.append(newInterval) adds the new interval to the list.
syntaxExplanations.4: intervals.sort() orders all intervals by their start value.
syntaxExplanations.5: merged = [] creates the empty result list.
syntaxExplanations.6: for i in range(len(intervals)): visits each interval by index.
syntaxExplanations.7: start = intervals[i][0] reads the current interval's start.
syntaxExplanations.8: end = intervals[i][1] reads the current interval's end.
syntaxExplanations.9: if len(merged) == 0: is true only for the very first interval.
syntaxExplanations.10: merged.append([start, end]) seeds the result with the first interval.
syntaxExplanations.12: last_end = merged[-1][1] reads the end of the last merged block.
syntaxExplanations.13: if start > last_end: is true when the current interval is disjoint.
syntaxExplanations.14: merged.append([start, end]) adds a new, non-overlapping block.
syntaxExplanations.16: if end > last_end: is true when the overlap extends the block further.
syntaxExplanations.17: merged[-1][1] = end stretches the last block to cover the overlap.
syntaxExplanations.18: return merged hands back the merged interval list.
